Subject: Audit log concordance & PII export question for SOC2 pack

Hi Logan / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our SOC2 auditor asked for a very specific scope check: they want a sample export showing the union of admin activity and operator actions for a 30-day window, with any PII redacted at the field level. Specifically they need to confirm:

- Which event types are captured (auth, token issuance, role changes, API calls, model loads, KV cache evictions, etc.)
- Field-level schemas (which fields may contain user identifiers or IPs)
- Default retention for admin events and an explanation of on-demand export options (format, delivery, manifest/hash)

Can you provide a short written response and a small sample (schema + 24h slice) we can include in the evidence bundle? If there are redaction knobs or sampling caveats we should call those out.

Also, what export delivery mechanisms do you support for customer-attested evidence (secure SFTP, presigned S3, signed manifests)?

Appreciate a reply by EOD Monday (10/4) if possible — auditor timeline.

Thanks,
Sally
Security Engineer, MediLabs

Hi Sally — thanks for the clear ask. Looping Kim (policy + compliance) and Ben (logs tooling) — we'll assemble a concise response and a 24-hour anonymized slice you can attach to the SOC2 bundle.

Quick answers up front:
- Event types: we capture auth (login/refresh/fail), token issuance, role grants/revocations, admin console actions (create/delete/config changes), API requests (route, model_id, response codes), model load/unload, KV cache operations and scheduled job executions.
- Fields that may contain identifiers: user_id, session_id, ip_address, resource_id, api_key_id. Those can be pseudonymized or redacted per your requirement.
- Retention: default admin event retention is 365 days. We support on-demand exports (ndjson) with signed manifest (SHA256) and delivery via presigned S3, secure SFTP, or encrypted TLS transfer.

Ben: can you attach the current audit schema CSV and a short playbook for export formats? Kim: can you draft a short paragraph about field-level redaction options we can share externally?

We should be able to get this to you well before EOD Monday.

Best,
Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: audit schema + suggested export playbook (for MediLabs)

Logan / Kim — attaching the two artifacts you asked for: audit_schema_v2.csv (field|type|sample) and export_playbook.pdf (delivery options + manifest examples). Highlights:

- Format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for event slices; separate manifest.json with file names, record counts, start/end timestamps and SHA256 checksums.
- Fields we consider PII/high-sensitivity: user_email, user_name, ip_address, user_id, api_key_id. We can pseudonymize user_email -> hash(email) and drop ip_address if required.
- Retention & granularity: default retention 365 days at full fidelity. For SOC2 evidence we'll typically provide a time-limited export containing only timestamps and event types unless customer requests identifiers for tracing.
- Delivery: presigned S3 (7-day expiry) or SFTP with host key verification. For high-assurance deliveries we provide an attested manifest signed with our private HMAC key; customer can verify SHA256 per-file.

Caveats:
- Live KV cache entries are not exported — we log cache operations (evict/load) and the keys referenced, but not cached payloads.
- Sampling: if a request is to supply a 30-day union we recommend either a full export (if within size budgets) or a stratified sample by event type to demonstrate coverage.

Attaching files: [audit_schema_v2.csv] [export_playbook.pdf]

- Ben
Principal Reliability Engineer

Hi Sally — sorry for the brief delay; thanks for the timeline and good questions. Below is the text you can include in evidence, plus pointers to the attached sample export (24h slice) and the schema.

Short summary for auditor (copyable):
Redwood Inference captures a comprehensive admin and operator activity ledger that includes authentication events, authorization changes (role/grant/revoke), console configuration changes, API request metadata (route, model_id, response status), model lifecycle events (load/unload/version pinning), KV cache operation metadata, and scheduled job execution records. Each event is timestamped (ISO8601), source (user_id or service_id), actor_role, event_type, and a free-form details blob for contextual fields.

Field-level sensitivity and redaction:
- Fields that may contain PII: user_email, user_name, ip_address, user_id. By default, exports include user_id (opaque GUID) and user_email is redacted to a hashed representation on request. IP addresses are redacted by default for exported evidence unless explicitly requested and approved via an SCC (secure control channel).
- Redaction options: full redaction (remove field), pseudonymization (sha256(email) with salt), or tokenization (replace with mapping table kept under customer request).

Retention & export mechanics:
- Default retention for admin/operator events: 365 days (configurable under Dedicated/Private plans).
- Export format: NDJSON (one JSON event per line); manifest.json accompanies exports and contains file-level SHA256 checksums and a signed HMAC token for verification.
- Delivery options: presigned S3 (recommended for large exports), secure SFTP with host-key verification, or direct HTTPS pull over a customer-managed pickup endpoint. We support generating timeboxed access tokens and delivering signed manifests for chain-of-custody.

Sampling guidance:
- For large tenants we recommend a stratified 30-day sample keyed by event_type to demonstrate coverage. For full forensic requests we can provide a full export (size/ingest costs may apply) with an agreed-upon retention slice.

Attached to this message: audit_schema_v2.csv (field list + sensitivity annotations) and export_playbook.pdf (examples: manifest schema, presigned S3 steps, SFTP host key guidance). I also included a 24-hour anonymized NDJSON slice in the playbook link for the auditor.

If the auditor wants a signed attest (HMAC of manifest) we can produce that and a delivery digest. Let me know your preferred delivery method (presigned S3 link or SFTP) and whether you need IP addresses included.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance Programs | Redwood Inference
